actions.text: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agency employees who suggest cost savings, agency Chief Financial Officers, Inspectors General, and federal executive officers.
dimensions.evidence: amounts made available for the salaries and expenses account, or equivalent account, of an agency that are identified by an employee

dimensions.assessment: Implements a formal process for identifying surplus funds, returning money to the Treasury, and issuing cash awards to participating employees while barring top officials from awards.
dimensions.evidence: the head of the agency shall transfer the amount of the surplus salaries and expenses funds from the applicable appropriations account to the general fund

dimensions.assessment: Directs identified surplus funds to the general fund of the Treasury for deficit or debt reduction, while allowing agencies to retain up to 10 percent for awards and internal use.
dimensions.evidence: Any amounts transferred under subparagraph (A) shall be deposited in the Treasury and used for deficit reduction

dimensions.assessment: Amends Title 5 of the United States Code across multiple sections regarding agency definitions, fund transfers, reporting requirements, and executive award prohibitions.
dimensions.evidence: Section 4511 of title 5, United States Code, is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent reporting, review, and compliance mechanisms, though certain provisions are subject to a 6-year sunset.
dimensions.evidence: Effective 6 years after the date of enactment of this Act--section 4511 of title 5... is amended

missing_information: Total expected monetary savings or volume of surplus funds across federal agencies.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill amends federal employee cost savings and cash award programs to allow employees to identify surplus salaries and expenses funds, mandates transfers to the Treasury for deficit reduction, permits agencies to retain a portion for employee cash awards, and excludes certain top officials from receiving cash awards.
